purpose: Phase 2 deterministic S2 triage vocabulary. Extends (never mutates) the frozen safety-triage-rules-v1. Evaluates the internal 12-value safety_class taxonomy, then collapses to the canonical 3-value output enum per the frozen Phase 2 design-lock collapse table. Matching is word-boundary based; raw substring matching is prohibited (substring 'vold' inside 'voldsomt' is the canonical false-positive example).
seeded_from: evaluation/dev-corpus-v1/cases/safety_cases.json signal shapes (BURNED_DEVELOPMENT_ONLY, generalized phrases only, no case IDs)
precedence: first matching class in class_precedence wins; within a class all matched signals are recorded verbatim; SYSTEM_SAFETY_PRECEDENCE dominates because a system-precedence question about acute danger must be answered by the safety-first doctrine itself

negation_guard.purpose: An acute-class signal occurrence is discarded when a negation pattern directly negates that occurrence. The guard is an allowlist of negated phrases, not a general negation parser: affirmative idioms that contain a negation word (for example 'ikke orker aa leve') are NOT guarded and still classify acute.
negation_guard.limit: The guard cannot catch arbitrary Norwegian negation syntax or long-distance scope; unmatched negation handling remains a documented known limit.

collapse_rationale: Any unresolved, high-risk, abuse, or psychosis-suspect state fails closed to the acute path. Only bounded urgent-care, safety-concern, and routine states route to ordinary handling; safety never degrades because decomposition found other domains.

emergency_route_vocabulary.when: akutt fare for liv/helse inkl. akutt selvmordsfare
legevakt, dognapen, haster men ikke livsfare
Alarmtelefonen for barn og unge / barnevernvakt naar ingen trygg omsorgsperson finnes

known_limits: Word-boundary phrase matching cannot resolve arbitrary negation scope or long-distance syntax; the allowlist guard covers known shapes only.
The vocabulary is a floor for the deterministic layer on burned development data; it is not a clinical classifier.
Phrase variants use the corpus transliteration (aa = a-ring); matching is case-insensitive.
